name: Mussaurus
sum: Mussaurus is a herbivorous sauropodomorph from the Early Jurassic of southern Argentina, named for its tiny juveniles and now known from adults up to 8 m long.
wsnote: Adults up to 8 m and 1.2-1.6 t (Wikipedia revision).
holotype: Not read in the sources consulted; the first nest with juveniles was described by Bonaparte and Vince in 1979.
material: Numerous specimens of varying age from one locality, juveniles to adults; adults were first described in 2013.
exceptional: A nest with eggs and hatchlings; many ages together at one site.
biology: Young were small quadrupeds and adults medium-sized bipeds. Many specimens of different ages at one locality suggest it was one of the earliest dinosaurs to live in groups.
author: Bonaparte and Vince 1979
